idiom_name: JSP tag file / JavaBean helper (the source's JavaBean and Custom Tag Helper strategies)
implementation_notes: The canonical realizations are the source's own strategies: a JavaBean placed in request scope by the controller (request.setAttribute, then <jsp:useBean>/EL) that exposes display-ready properties, or a custom tag that encapsulates iteration and formatting as a reusable element - modern Jakarta Pages packages such tags as tag files under /WEB-INF/tags. Use the bean form for pure adaptation and formatting, and the tag form when the helper must control markup structure (a table of rows) without scriptlets; a static formatting helper can also be published as an EL function in a tag library descriptor. Services stay behind a business delegate and the helper never reaches the database.
code_sketch: <%-- /WEB-INF/tags/money.tag --%> <%@ attribute name="amount" required="true" type="java.math.BigDecimal" %> <%@ taglib prefix="fmt" uri="jakarta.tags.fmt" %> <%-- view (no scriptlet): --%> <%-- controller: request.setAttribute("order", orderBean); --%>
pitfalls: A JavaBean helper that owns per-request state must be request-scoped; putting it in session scope leaks one user's data into another's page - the classic JSP helper bug.
EL silently coerces types (null to empty, BigDecimal to double), so a formatting helper can render 0.00 for missing data without raising anything.
A tag file's attribute directives are checked at render time, not build time: a mismatched attribute name or path fails the page, not the compilation.

variants.name: Thymeleaf expression utility objects with Spring beans (modern servlet stacks)
variants.idiom_name: Thymeleaf #numbers/#temporals/#strings utility objects plus registered expression objects
variants.implementation_notes: In a Spring Boot + Thymeleaf stack the view helper is the expression utility object: formatting is called inside the markup through #numbers.formatCurrency(...), #temporals.format(...) or #strings.*(...), and project-specific helpers are registered as additional expression objects (or invoked as Spring beans from the expression). Templates stay natural - they remain valid HTML - and the logic lives in Spring beans and services, so the classic helper class is unnecessary because the expression context already provides a helper namespace. Prefer the JSP tag-file variant only in maintenance-mode Jakarta Pages applications.
variants.code_sketch: - -
pitfalls: Expression utility calls are evaluated while rendering, so a helper that reaches a service from the expression runs once per row and bypasses the controller's transaction and caching.
Custom expression objects fail at render time until their dialect/configuration is registered; there is no build-time check that the template's helper exists.
Every object the controller puts into the model is reachable from the expression language, so exposing services 'for convenience' widens what a template can call.
